thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Entertainment separation: broken; board rejected minority listing [D01, D07]
Electronics recovery: broken; mobile goodwill impairment reflects lower expected future cash flows [D01, D03]
Structural catalyst: broken; original governance path rejected by board [D04, D07]
final.remaining_skew: downside risk of repeated electronics disappointment consuming asset cushion [D04]
final.next_catalyst_and_timing: none; no accepted restructuring timetable exists [D03, D07]

drivers.driver: The core investment catalyst—the separation of entertainment and electronics—has been explicitly rejected by the board [D01, D07].
Mobile business performance has deteriorated, evidenced by a ¥180bn goodwill impairment and a shift to a loss-making outlook [D01, D03].
The company has suspended its dividend, signaling restricted capital return prospects in the near term [D03, D04].
Operational recovery in the electronics division remains inconsistent, creating ongoing risks to the asset base [D04, D05].

final.memo:
Our original thesis for the Company was built upon a clear catalyst: the potential for a separation of the content-franchise value from the struggling electronics business to unlock hidden asset value [D07, D08]. With the board having officially rejected the proposed entertainment listing, this primary event-driven thesis is now broken [D03, D07]. We are unwilling to remain long based on hope for future management self-help when the governance path we identified has been explicitly closed [D04, D07].

Recent financial disclosures further degrade the investment case. The ¥180bn impairment of the mobile-communications business highlights a significant failure in the electronics division’s ability to generate reliable cash flows [D01, D03]. The downward revision of the full-year forecast from a ¥140bn profit to a ¥40bn loss underscores the reality that the business remains caught in a cycle of repeated disappointments [D01, D03, D04].

We do not wait to be proved right in the long run when the fundamental drivers of our exit strategy are spent [D04, D07]. The absence of an accepted IPO timetable or a viable plan to address the remaining sum-of-the-parts discount leaves us with inadequate upside relative to the risks of further capital erosion in the mobile segment [D03, D07]. We exit now to reallocate capital into higher-skew events where our edge is better defined and the catalyst remains intact [D04, D08].
